title: Final test: lessons 1–16
description: 20 hard questions on HTML, CSS and JavaScript

questions.prompt: What color will the text be?
questions.explain: An id outweighs a class, a class outweighs a tag: #main p beats .box p and p.

questions.prompt: The block has the default box-sizing (content-box). What is the full width of the box on screen?
questions.explain: 200 + 20 + 20 + 2 + 2 = 244px. With content-box, padding and border are added to width.

questions.prompt: The same card, but the CSS has * { box-sizing: border-box; }. What is the full width of the box?
questions.explain: With border-box, width includes padding and border, so the full width is 200px.

questions.prompt: What does margin: 10px 20px 30px; mean? What is the bottom margin?
questions.explain: Three values: top, left-right, bottom. Bottom = 30px.

questions.prompt: There are three blocks in the container. The last one has margin-top: auto. Where will the last block end up?
options: At the start, right under the first one
Pushed to the bottom of the container
questions.explain: margin-top: auto takes all the free space above the element and pushes it down.

questions.prompt: What are the widths of .a and .b?
questions.explain: Shares 1 + 2 = 3 parts of 100px: .a = 100px, .b = 200px.

questions.prompt: What is the width of one column?
The container is 1000px wide. What is the width of the 1fr column?
The browser window is exactly 600px wide. Will this rule apply?
options: No, only when the width is less than 600px
No, media queries don't work with px
questions.explain: max-width: 600px includes 600px.

questions.prompt: What is the padding of .header when the window is 400px wide?
questions.explain: Same specificity — the rule written later wins. Here it is .header { padding: 24px }.

questions.prompt: What happens to the width of the span?
options: It is ignored: span is inline
An error appears in the console
questions.explain: width doesn't work on inline elements; you need display: inline-block or block.

questions.prompt: A list of 6 items. Which items turn red?
questions.explain: Numbering starts at 1: odd means 1, 3, 5.

questions.prompt: What will be printed?
questions.explain: A historical JavaScript bug: typeof null returns "object".

questions.prompt: What will be printed?
questions.explain: == converts types, === compares both value and type.

questions.prompt: What will be printed?
questions.explain: 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004, so the comparison gives false.

questions.prompt: What will be printed?
questions.explain: const forbids reassignment, but the array contents can change.

questions.prompt: What will be printed?
questions.explain: The remainder takes the sign of the dividend: −5 = 2 × (−2) + (−1).

questions.prompt: What will be printed?
questions.explain: Curly braces after => are a code block. name becomes a label, and the function returns nothing.

questions.prompt: What will be printed?
questions.explain: map gives [2, 4, 6], filter keeps [4, 6].

questions.prompt: What will be printed?
questions.explain: find returns undefined if nothing is found. filter would return [].
